cues.text: Excuse me, Dr Thompson. May I speak to you for a minute?
cues.speaker: ALEXANDRA

cues.text: Of course. Please come in.
cues.speaker: MR THOMPSON

cues.text: I’m Alexandra Jones. I’m studying Business here at the university and for my assignment
cues.speaker: ALEXANDRA

cues.text: I have to carry out a survey of people who own their own organisations.
cues.speaker: ALEXANDRA

cues.text: I heard that you are the founder of your own company, and I was wondering if I could ask you some questions about it.
cues.speaker: ALEXANDRA

cues.text: Yes, of course, please fire away.
cues.speaker: MR THOMPSON

cues.text: OK great, we’ll get started! Did you encounter any problems whilst you were starting your company?
cues.speaker: ALEXANDRA

cues.text: Actually it was not as hard as I anticipated.
cues.speaker: MR THOMPSON

cues.text: I started out with very clear objectives, so I knew exactly what I wanted my corporate identity to be.
cues.speaker: MR THOMPSON

cues.text: It was very difficult to find the correct premises as the property market in London is so competitive, but eventually I found the perfect site.
cues.speaker: MR THOMPSON

cues.text: The hardest part was structuring the business, as I had no formal template so I had to create it myself.
cues.speaker: MR THOMPSON

cues.text: Yes, that is very impressive. Was it difficult dealing with staff?
cues.speaker: ALEXANDRA

cues.text: It’s always tricky trying to satisfy a group of people with varying interests, however, I didn’t encounter many problems.
cues.speaker: MR THOMPSON

cues.text: I found it very important to make the staff feel appreciated, so I hosted a staff day where we could all introduce ourselves and get to know each other as individuals.
cues.speaker: MR THOMPSON

cues.text: I was also able to talk to them about the type of work that they would be doing and gave them the opportunity to share with me the issues they had with the allocation of the work.
cues.speaker: MR THOMPSON

cues.text: OK. Did you hire a management team or did you take on the role of the manager?
cues.speaker: ALEXANDRA

cues.text: Oh no, I already had enough tasks to take care of.
cues.speaker: MR THOMPSON

cues.text: I employed someone else to take on the role of the manager, however, he never consulted me before making decisions so I was forced to let him go and hire someone else.
cues.speaker: MR THOMPSON

cues.text: And what did the other staff think of the new manager?
cues.speaker: ALEXANDRA

cues.text: They had a great deal of respect for him.
cues.speaker: MR THOMPSON

cues.text: It definitely helped that I consulted with them before hiring him.
cues.speaker: MR THOMPSON

cues.text: They were surprised that he has been so successful in his role at the company, despite the longer meeting hours.
cues.speaker: MR THOMPSON

cues.text: Since the company opened, has it had any great achievements?
cues.speaker: ALEXANDRA

cues.text: There are many aspects of the company that I am pleased with, however, there is one achievement of which I am particularly proud.
cues.speaker: MR THOMPSON

cues.text: I wanted a mural painted to brighten up our entrance area, so I decided it would be a great idea to invite the local primary school to create one for us.
cues.speaker: MR THOMPSON

cues.text: The youngsters had a great time and I know they were thrilled to be included.
cues.speaker: MR THOMPSON

cues.text: Oh, that’s lovely.
cues.speaker: ALEXANDRA

cues.text: Have you encountered any major problems since you opened the company?
cues.speaker: ALEXANDRA

cues.text: Yes, we are always encountering issues with employment because it is very hard to find people who are qualified for the roles that we were offering, but unfortunately there is no solution to this.
cues.speaker: MR THOMPSON

cues.text: One of our administrators also recently left to go on maternity leave, which put us in a tricky situation, however, we have managed to find a temporary replacement for her.
cues.speaker: MR THOMPSON

cues.text: It’s also now approaching the period when we must carry out our financial training so I need to find a venue with enough space to hold everyone.
cues.speaker: MR THOMPSON

cues.text: It will be interesting trying to organise that event!
cues.speaker: MR THOMPSON

cues.text: Oh gosh, I can imagine. I find it hard enough to organise myself!
cues.speaker: ALEXANDRA

cues.text: Organisation is a difficult thing to master, but it is also essential for success!
cues.speaker: MR THOMPSON

cues.text: Whilst I was learning how to stay organised, I realised that the role of motivation is essential.
cues.speaker: MR THOMPSON

cues.text: OK, that’s great!
cues.speaker: ALEXANDRA

cues.text: I also suggest that you visit the library, as there is a section on culture that will have some very valuable material on how to develop your organisation skills.
cues.speaker: MR THOMPSON

cues.text: OK, I’ll head to the library when we’re finished.
cues.speaker: ALEXANDRA

cues.text: I think you will find it very useful.
cues.speaker: MR THOMPSON

cues.text: They also have a collection of documentaries on the subject of personal organisation and I suggest that you look up the literature on management of change.
cues.speaker: MR THOMPSON

cues.text: I personally found these sources incredibly useful.
cues.speaker: MR THOMPSON

cues.text: Articles are also a valuable resource and we have a whole collection of them in our university library.
cues.speaker: MR THOMPSON

cues.text: I advise that you look at Section 2 where you will find articles on the nature of volunteering.
cues.speaker: MR THOMPSON

cues.text: That’s great, thank you so much for your help.
cues.speaker: ALEXANDRA

cues.text: No problem.
cues.speaker: MR THOMPSON
